mainTopic: How far a corpse's טומאה spreads, and who is sent home from war or kept from fleeing
overview: The amud opens with the rule that a מת 'takes up' four אמות for טומאה. It supports this with a משנה about a חצר הקבר, where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about its size. The גמרא flips that משנה's split between an entrance from above and an entrance from the side. It then limits the smaller sizes to a courtyard with clear walls. Next, the גמרא explains the war exemptions in דברים 20. A man who betrothed a woman goes home, and this includes a יבם whose יבמה is waiting for him, but not a man in a forbidden marriage. רבה's rule shows that even רבי יוסי הגלילי can agree with this. A ברייתא learns from the order of the פסוקים to build a house, plant a vineyard and only then marry, and it gives several readings of a פסוק in משלי about the order of learning and good deeds. The גמרא then explains which builders do not go home, and that a new husband stays home completely and may not even do support jobs. A new משנה brings רבי עקיבא, רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי יוסי on who counts as 'הירא ורך הלבב'. It then describes guards with iron rods who stop soldiers from fleeing, and this משנה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A corpse takes up four cubits for impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that a מת 'takes up' four אמות around it for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A dead body takes up four cubits around it when it comes to impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: the area of four אמות around a מת is treated as connected to it for טומאה. The next step brings a source that supports this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, טומאת מת passes through touching, carrying, or being under the same roof (אהל). This rule adds a safety zone: standing within four אמות of a מת is treated as a problem for טומאה. This protects people, like a כהן, who must stay away from טומאת מת.

keyTerms.meaning: A dead body
Takes up, occupies (an area)
Four cubits (about 2 meters)
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: A corpse takes up four cubits with regard to impurity.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The area of four אמות around a מת is treated as connected to it for טומאה.

steps.title: Support from the grave courtyard dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה about a חצר הקבר. בית שמאי require four אמות for someone standing inside to be טהור, and בית הלל say four טפחים are enough. The משנה then limits בית הלל's view to an entrance from above.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא also taught this: if someone stands inside the courtyard of a grave, he is pure, as long as the courtyard is four cubits in size. That is בית שמאי's view. בית הלל say four handbreadths are enough. When does this apply? When the entrance is from above. But if the entrance is from the side, everyone agrees the courtyard must be four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the four-אמות rule with a משנה about a courtyard next to a grave. It shows that size, measured in אמות, matters for whether someone standing near a grave becomes טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's four-אמות requirement fits the idea that a מת affects four אמות around it. בית הלל need only four טפחים. The משנה's last line says בית הלל's smaller size works only with an entrance from above, and that with a side entrance everyone agrees to four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our תנא taught': a source supports what was just said
The small walled courtyard in front of a burial cave
Handbreadths (a much smaller measure than אמות)
'When is this said?': a phrase that limits a ruling to certain cases
Its entrance

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי's 'four אמות' and בית הלל's 'four טפחים' sound alike but are very different sizes. An אמה is about six טפחים.

phrases.english: And our tanna also taught:
phrases.notes: The source quoted here is a משנה in אהלות.

phrases.english: A courtyard of a grave: one who stands inside it is pure,
provided that it has four cubits in it,
these are the words of Beit Shammai.
Beit Hillel say: four handbreadths.
When is this said? When its entrance is from above,
but if its entrance is from the side,
everyone agrees it must be four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up the four-אמות rule of step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a מת takes up four אמות for טומאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in אהלות about the חצר הקבר, where a four-אמות measure decides whether someone standing inside is טהור.

steps.title: The entrance split seems backwards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's split is upside down. A side entrance lets a person slip out safely, but entering from above makes it almost impossible not to pass over the grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which way is this going?! It's the opposite! From the side, a person can slip away and leave. From above, it is impossible that he won't hover over the grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last line of the משנה. It says the משנה's logic about which entrance is more dangerous is reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a side entrance, a person can slide along the wall and leave without being over the grave. Climbing down from above, his body will almost surely end up over the grave and make an אהל, which makes him טמא. So the entrance from above should be the stricter case, needing four אמות, not the easier one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Which way is this going?!': a sharp way of saying 'you have it backwards'
On the contrary
Slips away and goes out
Forms an אהל, covering or hovering over the טומאה

phrases.english: Which way is this going?!
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא says: you've got it backwards!

phrases.english: On the contrary: from the side, he slips away and leaves,
from above, it is impossible that he will not overlie the grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'במה דברים אמורים' line at the end of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that בית הלל's four טפחים apply to an entrance from above, while a side entrance needs four אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Entering from above is more dangerous because the person will pass over the grave, so it should need the larger size. The משנה's split looks reversed.

steps.title: Flipping the entrance split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewrites the משנה's line. בית הלל's four טפחים apply when the entrance is from the side. With an entrance from above, everyone requires four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say it this way: when does this apply? When the entrance is from the side. But if the entrance is from above, it must be four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge by reversing the משנה's split, so it matches the logic of step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the easier rule (four טפחים, by בית הלל) goes with the safer entrance from the side. The stricter rule (four אמות, agreed by everyone) goes with the risky entrance from above.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': brings a corrected version or a new approach

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִן הַצַּד,
phrases.english: Rather: when is this said? When its entrance is from the side,
but if its entrance is from above, it must be four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים שֶׁפִּתְחָהּ מִן הַצַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by reversing the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the source: the two cases in the 'במה דברים אמורים' line are switched.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to make the entrance from above the easier case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The entrance from the side is the easier case (four טפחים by בית הלל). The entrance from above needs four אמות according to everyone.

steps.title: Small sizes apply only to a walled courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a limit. The smaller sizes apply only to a חצר הקבר with clear walls. An ordinary מת lying in the open always takes up four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to a grave courtyard whose walls are clearly marked. But an ordinary corpse does take up four cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up this topic. It explains why the courtyard can be smaller than four אמות without weakening the basic rule from step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walls that mark off the courtyard make it a separate space, so a smaller area can be enough there. A מת without such walls still has its full four-אמות zone. That is how the courtyard case fits with the rule in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And these words apply only to': a phrase that limits a rule
Its partitions are clearly marked off
Ordinary, in general

steps.whatToRemember: A מת takes up four אמות for טומאה. Inside a walled חצר הקבר a smaller space can be enough: four טפחים with a side entrance according to בית הלל, but four אמות with an entrance from above. A מת in the open always keeps its four אמות.

phrases.english: And these words apply to a grave courtyard
whose partitions are clearly marked,
but an ordinary corpse does take up [four cubits].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי, חֲצַר הַקֶּבֶר דִּמְסַיְּימָא מְחִיצָתַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the courtyard sizes to a walled courtyard, which keeps the four-אמות rule of step 1 in place.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The smaller courtyard sizes are a special case for a walled חצר הקבר. A מת without walls around it takes up four אמות.

steps.title: Which betrothed men go home from the army
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's פסוק of 'מי האיש אשר ארש אשה'. A ברייתא explains that it includes a man who betrothed a בתולה, a man who betrothed an אלמנה, and a יבם whose יבמה is waiting for him. If one of five brothers dies in war, all the other brothers go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who is the man that has betrothed a woman...' The Rabbis taught: 'that has betrothed' means one who betroths a virgin, one who betroths a widow, and one for whom a widow is waiting for יבום. Even if there are five brothers and one of them dies in the war, they all go home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה: the men who are sent home before battle. It brings a ברייתא that explains who counts as 'a man who betrothed a woman.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'אשר ארש' broadly. It covers a man who betrothed a בתולה or an אלמנה, and also a man connected to a woman through יבום. Since any one of the surviving brothers could do the יבום, all of them go home.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothed (made the first stage of marriage)
'The Rabbis taught': opens a ברייתא
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום
Return (go home from the army)

steps.confusionAlert: 'שומרת יבם' here means the man is the brother-in-law the widow is waiting for. He has not betrothed her, but he still counts and goes home.

phrases.english: "What man is there that has betrothed a wife, etc."
The Rabbis taught: "that has betrothed"
means both one who betroths a virgin,
and one who betroths a widow,
and one for whom a widow is waiting for yibum.
And even if there are five brothers,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם בַּמִּלְחָמָה — כּוּלָּן חוֹזְרִין.
phrases.english: and one of them dies in the war, they all return home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the טומאה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אשר ארש' includes a man who betrothed a בתולה or an אלמנה, and a יבם with a waiting יבמה. If one of five brothers dies in war, all the other brothers go home.

steps.title: Forbidden marriages do not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses the words 'ולא לקחה' to exclude men whose betrothal is forbidden, such as an אלמנה to a כהן גדול or a גרושה to a כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Not taken,' 'and has not taken her': this excludes a widow betrothed to a כהן גדול, a divorcee or חלוצה betrothed to an ordinary כהן, a ממזרת or נתינה betrothed to a regular Jew, and a Jewish woman betrothed to a ממזר or a נתין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and sets a limit. The exemption from war is only for a man betrothed to a woman he is allowed to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'her,' meaning a woman who is fit to be 'taken' by him. A man in a marriage the תורה forbids does not get this exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And has not taken her' (married her fully)
'Excluding': this case is left out
A widow released from יבום through חליצה
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול
A descendant of the גבעונים, whom a regular Jew may not marry

steps.whatToRemember: Only a man betrothed to a woman he may marry is sent home. Forbidden marriages are excluded.

phrases.english: "Not taken," "and has not taken her":
phrases.notes: The extra word 'her' points to a woman he is actually allowed to take.

phrases.english: this excludes a widow betrothed to a High Priest,
a divorcee or a chalutza betrothed to an ordinary priest,
a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman betrothed to an Israelite,
an Israelite woman betrothed to a mamzer or to a Gibeonite.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא לָקַח, וְלֹא לְקָחָהּ — פְּרָט לְאַלְמָנָה לַכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by setting a limit on the men described in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man betrothed in a forbidden marriage does not go home from war because of his betrothal.

steps.title: Does this disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He explains 'הירא ורך הלבב' as a man afraid of his own sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this ברייתא is not like רבי יוסי הגלילי? Because רבי יוסי הגלילי says that 'the fearful and fainthearted' means a man who is afraid because of the sins he has done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible conflict between the ברייתא and the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, a man with sins goes home as 'הירא ורך הלבב.' A man in a forbidden marriage is a sinner, so he should go home anyway. The ברייתא, though, treats him as excluded from going home, so the two views seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say': suggests a possible conclusion, often to be rejected
A תנא who explains 'הירא' as fear of sins
'The fearful and fainthearted' man, who is sent home from war
The sins he has done

phrases.english: Shall we say this is not in line with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הָא אָמַר
phrases.english: for if it were Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, he says:
"The fearful and fainthearted":
this is one who is afraid because of the sins he has done?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the exclusion in step 7 fits the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא excluding forbidden marriages must disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי, who sends a man afraid of his sins home as 'הירא ורך הלבב.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's exclusion (step 7) of a man betrothed in a forbidden marriage from going home.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, a man afraid of his sins goes home as 'הירא ורך הלבב'. A man in a forbidden betrothal is a sinner, so by him he should go home, which seems to contradict the ברייתא's exclusion.

steps.title: Even רבי יוסי הגלילי agrees, based on רבה's rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can fit even רבי יוסי הגלילי, because a man is only punished for a forbidden marriage once he lives with the woman, not for the betrothal alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, it works the way רבה explained. רבה said: a man is never liable until he lives with her. Why? The Torah's 'he shall not take' is there because of 'he shall not profane.' So he is not given lashes until he lives with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8. It shows that the ברייתא does not have to argue with רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was this: by רבי יוסי הגלילי, a man who betrothed a forbidden woman is a sinner, so he should go home as one who is 'afraid of his sins.' רבה teaches that the real sin is living with her, not the betrothal itself. So betrothal alone does not yet make him that kind of sinner, and the ברייתא can still leave him out.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say: the answer works even according to that view
Receives lashes as a punishment
He shall not profane: a כהן must not make his children unfit
Until he lives with her as husband and wife

steps.whatToRemember: For forbidden marriages of a כהן, the punishable act is living together, not the betrothal. This is why even רבי יוסי הגלילי can agree with the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
it works like Rabba's teaching.
For Rabba said:
He is never liable until he lives with her.
What is the reason? "He shall not take" is because of "he shall not profane";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:14–15. These are the פסוקים about whom a כהן גדול may not marry.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה עַד שֶׁיִּבְעוֹל.
phrases.english: therefore he does not get lashes until he lives with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, כִּדְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in an outside rule (רבה) that changes when the sin actually happens
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to argue with רבי יוסי הגלילי, since by him a forbidden betrothal makes a man a sinner who goes home
steps.terutzMaskana: The sin is only in living together, so betrothal alone does not send him home even by רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: The Torah teaches the right order: house, vineyard, then wife
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the order of the פסוקים that a person should first build a house, then plant a vineyard, and only then marry. A פסוק from שלמה says the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'who built,' 'who planted,' 'who betrothed.' The Torah taught good conduct: a person should build a house, plant a vineyard, and after that marry a wife. שלמה also said in his wisdom: 'Prepare your work outside, make it ready for yourself in the field, afterward build your house.' 'Work outside' is a house, 'the field' is a vineyard, 'build your house' is a wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that learns a life lesson from the order of the three cases in the army פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists the men in a set order: built a house, planted a vineyard, betrothed a woman. The ברייתא says this order is a lesson: first make sure you have a home and a way to earn a living, then get married. The פסוק in משלי backs up the same order.

keyTerms.meaning: Proper, sensible behavior
The Rabbis taught: opens a ברייתא
Prepare your work outside (משלי 24:27)
Vineyard: a source of income

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Who built," "who planted," "who betrothed":
the Torah taught proper conduct:
that a person should build a house, and plant a vineyard,
and after that marry a wife.
And Shlomo also said in his wisdom:
"Prepare your work outside,"
"and make it ready for yourself in the field,"
"afterward build your house."
"Prepare your work outside": this is a house.
"Make it ready for yourself in the field": this is a vineyard.
"Afterward build your house": this is a wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the legal question and opens an aggadic lesson about the same פסוקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should build a house, plant a vineyard, and then marry

steps.title: Another reading: מקרא, then משנה, then גמרא
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק is read as the order of Torah learning: first מקרא, then משנה, then גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Prepare your work outside' is מקרא. 'Make it ready in the field' is משנה. 'Afterward build your house' is גמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second way to read שלמה's פסוק, this time about the order of learning Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three parts of the פסוק become three stages of learning. First learn the written Torah, then the משנה, and only after that the deep give-and-take of גמרא, which 'builds the house' of understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: Another explanation
The written Torah (תנ"ך)
Deep study and reasoning behind the משנה

phrases.english: Another explanation:
"Prepare your work outside": this is מקרא.
"Make it ready for yourself in the field": this is משנה.
"Afterward build your house": this is גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״הָכֵן בַּחוּץ מְלַאכְתֶּךָ״ — זֶה מִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah learning goes in order: מקרא, משנה, then גמרא

steps.title: A third reading: learning first, then good deeds
steps.stepSummary: Another reading combines מקרא and משנה as the first stage and puts גמרא second. Good deeds are the final 'building.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'Prepare your work outside' is מקרא and משנה. 'Make it ready in the field' is גמרא. 'Afterward build your house' is good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא offers a third reading, where the last stage is not more learning but doing good deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the stages shift down by one. The two kinds of basic learning are grouped together, גמרא moves to the middle, and the goal at the end becomes מעשים טובים, putting the learning into action.

keyTerms.meaning: Good deeds

phrases.english: Another explanation:
"Prepare your work outside": this is מקרא and משנה.
"Make it ready for yourself in the field": this is גמרא.
"Afterward build your house": these are good deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״הָכֵן בַּחוּץ מְלַאכְתֶּךָ״ — זֶה מִקְרָא וּמִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading that shifts each stage and ends with good deeds
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning (מקרא, משנה, גמרא) comes first, and good deeds are the goal

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's reading: learning, good deeds, then teaching and reward
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי puts all learning first, then good deeds, and at the end teaching Torah and getting reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי says: 'Prepare your work outside' is מקרא, משנה and גמרא. 'Make it ready in the field' is good deeds. 'Afterward build your house' means: teach and receive reward.
steps.whatsHappening: A named תנא gives a fourth reading of the פסוק, ending with teaching Torah and earning reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three kinds of learning are now the first stage, and good deeds are the second. The last stage is דרוש, explaining Torah and drawing out new ideas, which a person may only do after building up both knowledge and good deeds.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain and draw out the meaning of the Torah
And receive reward

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק from משלי, four readings: house, vineyard, wife; or stages of learning that build up to good deeds and finally teaching Torah.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says:

phrases.aramaic: ״הָכֵן בַּחוּץ מְלַאכְתֶּךָ״ — זֶה מִקְרָא וּמִשְׁנָה וּגְמָרָא,
phrases.english: "Prepare your work outside": this is מקרא, משנה and גמרא.
"Make it ready for yourself in the field": these are good deeds.
"Afterward build your house": teach and receive reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of the readings of the פסוק, said by a named תנא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning, then good deeds, then teaching Torah and receiving reward

steps.title: Rebuilding a house: one new row of stones sends him home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of men who do not go home. A תנא adds that if a man rebuilding a house adds even one new row of stones, he does go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: these do not go home: one who builds a gatehouse, and so on. A תנא taught: if he added one row of stones to it, he goes home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, to the men who do NOT go home from the army, and adds a short teaching from a תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the part of the משנה cut short by 'כו׳', רבי יהודה says that a man who rebuilds a house exactly as it stood before does not go home. The תנא adds a limit: if he adds even one new row of stones, it counts as a new building, and he goes home.

keyTerms.meaning: Gatehouse: a small entry building
A row of stones in a wall
Goes home from the army
A תנא taught: introduces a short ברייתא

phrases.english: And these are the ones who do not go home:
one who builds a gatehouse, etc.
A תנא taught:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הוֹסִיף בּוֹ דִּימוֹס אֶחָד — חוֹזֵר.
phrases.english: If he added one row of stones to it, he goes home.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵינָן חוֹזְרִין: הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית שַׁעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the aggadah to the משנה's legal list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding even one new row of stones makes it a new house, so he goes home

steps.title: Brick houses in the שרון don't send a man home
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says a man who builds a brick house in the שרון does not go home. A תנא explains that these houses are rebuilt twice every seven years.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: even one who builds a brick house in the שרון would not go home. A תנא taught: because they rebuild it twice in seven years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and brings a תנא who gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא explains that brick houses in the שרון had to be rebuilt twice every seven years. Such a house is not a lasting home, so building one does not count as 'building a house' that sends a man back.

keyTerms.meaning: A house made of bricks
A region in ארץ ישראל
Here: a seven-year period

steps.confusionAlert: שבוע here does NOT mean a week of seven days. It means a cycle of seven years, like the שמיטה cycle.
steps.whatToRemember: A building only sends a man home if it is a real, lasting new house. A gatehouse, a rebuild with nothing new added, or a short-lived brick house in the שרון does not count.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית לְבֵנִים בַּשָּׁרוֹן — לֹא הָיָה חוֹזֵר.
phrases.english: Even one who builds a brick house in the Sharon would not go home.
A תנא taught:
Because they rebuild it twice in seven years.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַף הַבּוֹנֶה בֵּית לְבֵנִים בַּשָּׁרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through the משנה's list of men who do not go home
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A brick house in the שרון is not lasting, since it is rebuilt twice in seven years, so its builder does not go home

steps.title: A new husband is exempt even if he married a widow or a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about men who do not leave home. A ברייתא then learns that the word 'wife' covers a widow or a divorcée too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that some men do not even leave their places, such as one who built a house and dedicated it. The Rabbis taught: 'A new wife' could mean only a never-married woman. How do we know a widow or a divorcée also counts? The פסוק says 'a wife', meaning any wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting the משנה, then brings a ברייתא about the new husband in דברים 24:5. The ברייתא shows that his exemption applies no matter whom he married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'new wife' might suggest only a first-time bride. The ברייתא points out that the פסוק also says just 'wife', which is general. So a widow or a divorcée is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Move from their places; these men do not even go out to help the army
A new wife (דברים 24:5)
A widow
A divorcée
In any case; with no limits

phrases.english: And these are the ones who do not move from their places:
phrases.notes: Unlike the men who are sent home from battle but still bring supplies to the army, these men stay home completely.

phrases.english: One who built a new house and dedicated it, etc.
The Rabbis taught: "A new wife"
I would have only a new wife;
from where do we know a widow or a divorcée?
The verse says: "A wife", meaning any wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's next list (men who do not move at all) after the discussion of the שרון houses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A new husband's exemption applies even if his bride is a widow or a divorcée.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'new'?
steps.stepSummary: If any wife counts, the word 'new' seems to add nothing. The ברייתא asks what it teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'a new wife'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about the word 'new', which now looks extra. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'wife' already includes everyone, the word 'new' must have its own job. The question pushes us to find a case that 'new' leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
Why does the verse say this? What is it teaching?

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִשָּׁה חֲדָשָׁה״?
phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "a new wife"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the extra word 'new' adds, given the conclusion of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'new' comes to teach.

steps.title: 'New' means new to him, so remarrying an ex-wife does not count
steps.stepSummary: 'New' means a wife who is new to this man. A man who remarries his own divorcée is not exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means one who is new to him. This leaves out a man who remarries his divorced wife, since she is not new to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'new' is measured from the husband's side. A man who takes back his ex-wife does not get the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a widow or a divorcée does not matter. What matters is whether the marriage is a fresh start for this man. His own former wife is not new to him, so he must go to war.

keyTerms.meaning: One who remarries his own divorced wife

steps.whatToRemember: 'Wife' includes widows and divorcées, and 'new' means new to him. So only a man who remarries his own ex-wife loses the exemption.

phrases.english: One who is new to him;
this excludes one who takes back his divorcée,
who is not new to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'New' means new to the husband, which excludes a man who remarries his own divorcée.

steps.title: The new husband may not even do support jobs for the army
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the new husband does not even bring water and food or fix roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'He shall not go out with the army.' You might think he only does not go to battle, but he still brings water and food and fixes the roads. So the verse says: 'Neither shall he be charged with any business.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא explains how far the new husband's exemption goes. He is free from every army job, not just fighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the פסוק only forbids going out 'with the army', which might mean fighting alone. The second part, 'any business', shows he is free from support work too. This is why he 'does not move from his place.'

keyTerms.meaning: He shall not go out with the army
He supplies water and food
Neither shall he be charged with any business (דברים 24:5)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "He shall not go out with the army."
You might think it is only with the army that he does not go out,
but he would still supply water and food
and repair the roads;

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבֹר עָלָיו לְכׇל דָּבָר״.
phrases.english: the verse says: "Neither shall he be charged with any business."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא on the same פסוק, now about how far the exemption reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new husband is exempt from all army service, including supplying food and water and fixing roads.

steps.title: Only the new husband is free from support jobs, not the other exempt men
steps.stepSummary: The word 'him' limits this full exemption to the new husband. Others, like a man who built a house he has not dedicated, still do support work.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think we also include one who built a house and did not dedicate it, one who planted a vineyard and did not yet use its fruit, or one who betrothed a woman and did not marry her. So the verse says 'him': you do not charge him, but you do charge others.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and asks whether this full exemption also covers the other exempt men. It answers no, based on the word 'him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עָלָיו, 'upon him', points to this specific man, the one already married. The other exempt men skip the fighting but still help the army with supplies. This matches the משנה's two lists: those who return and help, and those who do not move at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Include; widen the rule to cover more cases
Redeemed it, so he may now use its fruit (the vineyard's fourth-year fruit)
Betrothed (but has not yet married)
Upon him; only this specific man

phrases.english: You might think that I include
even one who built a house and did not dedicate it,
one who planted a vineyard and did not redeem its fruit,
one who betrothed a woman and did not marry her;
the verse says: "him";
him you do not charge,
but you do charge others.
phrases.notes: 'Others' means these other exempt men. They skip the fighting but still bring supplies and fix roads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the full exemption of step 19 to the new husband alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the married new husband is free from support jobs; the other exempt men still serve in support roles.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need both phrases?
steps.stepSummary: If 'he shall not be charged with any business' already covers everything, the phrase 'he shall not go out with the army' looks extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah wrote 'neither shall he be charged', why do I need 'he shall not go out with the army'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the פסוק for seeming to repeat itself. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broad phrase already forbids every army job, and fighting is one of them. So the narrower phrase about going out with the army seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: And since it is written
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And since it is written: "Neither shall he be charged,"
why do I need "He shall not go out with the army"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the first phrase, given how step 19 reads the second phrase.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The broad prohibition already includes going out to war, so the specific phrase seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Two prohibitions for going to war
steps.stepSummary: The extra phrase means that if the new husband goes to battle, he breaks two prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he violates two prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra phrase is not wasted. It adds a second prohibition for the act of actually going to war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Support jobs are forbidden by one prohibition. Actually going out with the army breaks both phrases, so there are two לאוין for that act.

keyTerms.meaning: Two negative commandments (prohibitions)

steps.whatToRemember: The new husband is fully free from army service. If he goes out to fight anyway, he breaks two prohibitions.

phrases.english: So that he violates two prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra phrase adds a second prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'shall not go out with the army' is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: It makes going to battle a violation of two prohibitions.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the fearful man is simply afraid of battle
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה quotes the officers' last call. רבי עקיבא reads 'fearful and fainthearted' literally.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'And the officers shall speak further to the people...' רבי עקיבא says: 'Fearful and fainthearted' means just what it says: a man who cannot stand in the battle lines and see a drawn sword.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the last group sent home: the fearful man. רבי עקיבא says this means someone who is truly scared of fighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the word 'fear' has its plain meaning: fear of war itself. Such a man would not stand firm in battle, so he goes home.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
The fearful and fainthearted (דברים 20:8)
As it sounds; in its plain meaning
A drawn sword

phrases.english: MISHNA:
"And the officers shall speak further to the people, etc."
Rabbi Akiva says:
"Fearful and fainthearted" means what it says:
one who cannot stand in the battle lines
and see a drawn sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about the last group sent home from war.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'fearful' man is one who is truly afraid of battle.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the fearful man is afraid because of his sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי says the fearful man fears his sins. The other exemptions give him a cover so he can leave without shame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: 'Fearful and fainthearted' is one who is afraid because of the sins he has done. That is why the Torah gave him all these other reasons, so he can go back because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees with רבי עקיבא. He says the fear is about a man's own sins, which could harm him in battle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only sinners left, everyone would know who they were. So the Torah also sends home the house-builder, the vineyard-planter and the new husband, and the sinner can blend in with them. This protects his honor.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is afraid because of sins
The Torah gave him something to blame; a cover story
Because of them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"Fearful and fainthearted":
this is one who is afraid because of the sins in his hands;

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ תָּלְתָה לוֹ הַתּוֹרָה אֶת כׇּל אֵלּוּ,
phrases.english: therefore the Torah gave him all these to blame,
phrases.notes: 'All these' are the other men sent home: the house-builder, the vineyard-planter and the man who betrothed a woman.

phrases.english: so that he can return because of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא about what kind of fear is meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'fearful' man fears his sins; the other exemptions let him leave without being exposed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This view explains why the Torah lists so many reasons to go home: they also protect the sinner from public shame.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: a man in a forbidden marriage is the fearful one
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי gives concrete examples of the sin meant: being betrothed to a woman who is forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A widow with a כהן גדול, a divorcée or a חלוצה with a regular כהן, a ממזרת or a נתינה with a regular Jew, or a Jewish woman with a ממזר or a נתין: that man is the 'fearful and fainthearted.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי names specific sins that make a man 'fearful'. They are all forbidden marriages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי יוסי הגלילי, he links fear to sin. But he names one specific kind of sin: being betrothed to a woman forbidden to him. Such a man is the one the פסוק calls 'הירא ורך הלבב'.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A widow released from יבום through חליצה
A woman born from a forbidden union
A woman or man descended from the גבעונים, who may not marry a regular Jew

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי here is a different תנא from רבי יוסי הגלילי in the step before. They are two separate people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
a widow with a High Priest,
phrases.notes: He is listing men betrothed to a woman they are forbidden to marry.

phrases.english: a divorcée or a chalutza with a regular priest,
a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman with an Israelite,
a daughter of Israel with a mamzer or a Gibeonite;
that man is the fearful and fainthearted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, more specific view: the sin meant is a forbidden marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man in a forbidden betrothal is the 'fearful and fainthearted' who goes home.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views of 'fearful': רבי עקיבא says fear of battle, רבי יוסי הגלילי says fear of one's sins, and רבי יוסי says the sin of a forbidden marriage.

steps.title: Captains are appointed at the front and the rear
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes the פסוק about appointing captains at the head of the people and adds that captains stand at the rear of the people too.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And when the officers finish speaking to the people, they shall appoint captains of legions at the head of the people." And also at the back of the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next stage of the war procedure: after the שוטרים finish their announcements, captains are put in place. It quotes the פסוק and then adds that captains also stand at the back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only mentions captains "at the head of the people." The משנה adds "and at the rear of the people," so leaders are placed at both ends of the army. This sets up the next line, which explains what the people at the front and back actually do.

keyTerms.meaning: Officers who made the announcements to the army
They appointed
Captains of legions, the army commanders
Its heel, meaning the back or rear

phrases.english: "And it shall be, when the officers finish
speaking to the people,
that they shall appoint captains of legions at the head of the people."
And also at the rear of the people.
phrases.notes: These words aren't in the פסוק. The משנה is adding that captains stand at the back too.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה כְּכַלֹּת הַשֹּׁטְרִים לְדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה after the discussion of who is exempt, moving to what happens once the announcements are done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the announcements, captains are appointed both at the head and at the rear of the army.

steps.title: Guards with iron rods stop soldiers from fleeing
steps.stepSummary: Guards are stationed in front of and behind the soldiers with iron rods. Anyone who tries to run away may be struck on the legs.
steps.simpleTranslation: They place guards in front of them and others behind them, with iron rods in their hands. Anyone who tries to turn back, the guard has permission to strike his legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the army keeps order: guards stand at the front and back holding iron rods. A soldier who tries to flee may be hit on the legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, anyone who wanted to leave had a proper chance to go home through the exemptions. Once the army is set, that chance is over, so running away is stopped by force. Striking the legs stops a soldier from fleeing, which could cause others to panic.

keyTerms.meaning: Guards who stand upright on watch
Iron rods or axes
He has permission
To strike or break
His legs, his shins

steps.whatToRemember: The exemptions give every exempt soldier a respectable way to leave before battle. After the army is arranged, no one may run away, and guards enforce this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the contrast in the procedure: generous exemptions first, then strict discipline once the army is formed.

phrases.english: They station guards in front of them
and others behind them,
with iron rods in their hands.
And anyone who tries to turn back,
he has permission to strike his legs.
phrases.notes: The "he" with permission is the guard, not the soldier running away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what is done at the front and rear of the army, building on the placement of captains in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guards with iron rods stand in front of and behind the army and may strike the legs of anyone who tries to flee.
